solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drug-led artist in crossover style

blocks.note: bhang is Indian hemp, a cannabis preparation
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter on drugs works in a style that blends genres.
explanation.walkthrough: '-led' tells you the drug comes first, with the artist after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhangra is a music style mixing Punjabi folk with Western pop, a crossover genre.

clue.text: Cop's jumping obstacles for US teenagers

blocks.note: a bobby is a British policeman
an oxer is a showjumping fence

explanation.surface: A police officer's horse-jumping fences.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British police officer; an oxer is a showjumping fence of rails, originally to keep in oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby-soxers were American teenage girls of the 1940s, named after their ankle socks.

clue.text: Cheer following tart round dance

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the cheer is placed behind the other piece

blocks.note: ho is slang for a prostitute
rah is a cry of encouragement

explanation.surface: Applause comes after a pastry is passed round at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the cheer after the tart. 'Tart' tempts as pastry but is slang for a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: The horah is a Romanian and Israeli folk dance performed in a circle.

clue.text: Coffee from the fringes of Colombia after an early harvest

indicators.note: the fringes of a word are its outermost letters

blocks.note: rabi is the spring harvest in India; 'an' gives A
the first and last letters of Colombia

explanation.surface: Coffee from the edges of Colombia, after picking the beans early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the Colombia letters behind A RABI.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabica is the main species of coffee plant and the beans it yields.

clue.text: Greek island temple with cross inside

indicators.note: one element is placed within the other

blocks.note: a naos is the inner sanctuary of a Greek temple
x is a cross mark

explanation.surface: A Greek island temple with a cross inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes inside NAOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Naxos is the largest of the Cyclades in the Aegean.

clue.text: Wine: a dash of red with chicken is set before husband

indicators.note: a mere dash is only a small amount, the opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of red
a hen is a chicken
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A recipe of wine, a splash of red and chicken is served before the husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenish is wine from the Rhine region, especially hock.

clue.text: Telegraphy switching parts of battle plan

indicators.note: the two halves of the word trade places, front going to the back

blocks.note: a tactic is a plan for a battle

explanation.surface: Signals are sent by swapping sections of a military plan.
explanation.walkthrough: TAC-TIC with its halves swapped reads TIC-TAC. Tic-tac is the hand-signal code bookmakers use at British racecourses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tic-tac is a system of arm signals passing betting odds across a racecourse, a kind of manual telegraph.

clue.text: Drunk up about a quarter of pint at most

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
a four-letter word's quarter is a single letter, here its first
about means around, so one part wraps the other

blocks.note: a sot is a drunkard
one of the four letters of pint

explanation.surface: A drinker downed a quarter of a pint at the very most.
explanation.walkthrough: SOT turned upward is TOS, which goes around P.
explanation.definitionFit: Tops, as in 'two hours tops', is informal for at the maximum.

clue.text: Fizz, tons taken about first in race. Ascot perhaps?

indicators.note: the first letter in the next word is the one used
the first parts are taken around the other letter

blocks.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
T is the abbreviation for tons
the first letter of race

explanation.surface: Champagne flows by the ton at the races at Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside CAVA-T after its C. Ascot is a famous English racecourse, but an ascot is also a broad necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a wide scarf-like necktie, a type of cravat, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Weight of old wool on top of old bustle

blocks.note: a tod was an old unit of weight for wool, about 28 pounds
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A load of antique wool sits on a Victorian dress bustle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top of' places TOD above O in this down entry. 'Bustle' looks like the dress padding but means commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or commotion, the same as a bustle of activity.

clue.text: Protean US creature mounting a rostrum

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means climbing, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a bema is a speaker's platform

explanation.surface: An American shape-shifting animal climbs onto a podium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ameba is the American spelling of amoeba, a single-celled organism that constantly changes shape.

clue.text: Source of bird seed, kilo lost from bursting granary sacks

indicators.note: a thing lost is no longer there, so that letter is removed
bursting sacks spill and scatter, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: K is the abbreviation for kilo, the letter to drop
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Birdseed spills from split sacks in a granary, a kilo of it lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the K from granary sacks, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Canary grass is a plant whose seed is a staple food for caged birds.

clue.text: Broom fashioned in tea-tree or chocolate tree

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged
one part sits inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of broom, rearranged
Thea is the botanical genus name once given to the tea plant

explanation.surface: A broom made of tea-tree or cacao wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled broom goes inside THE-A, the old genus name of the tea plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Theobroma is the genus of the cacao tree whose beans give chocolate.

clue.text: Good place for open-air theatre? Paid misguidedly with wind around

indicators.note: a misguided thing goes the wrong way, so its letters stray from order
one part encircles the other

blocks.note: Eurus is the Greek god of the east wind
the letters of paid, rearranged

explanation.surface: An outdoor theatre was paid for wrongly, and the wind blew around it.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled paid sits inside EURUS, after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidaurus in Greece has a famous ancient open-air theatre, so it is an example of such a venue.

clue.text: Diseased sheep unknown in pound

indicators.note: one element is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to bray is to pound or crush, as in a mortar
x is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Sick sheep of unknown origin are kept in an animal pound.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes inside BRAY. 'Pound' looks like an enclosure for strays but is the verb meaning to crush.
explanation.definitionFit: Braxy is a Scottish term for an often fatal bacterial disease of sheep, and also for a sheep suffering from it.

clue.text: Left port with cargo aboard

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for left
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship sailed from port loaded with goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left port' reads as a ship departing, but it is L plus a named harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A laden vessel is loaded, carrying a full freight on board.

clue.text: Clumsy mistake involving an asset

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it inside, wrapping it

blocks.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
a boon is a benefit or asset; 'an' gives A

explanation.surface: An awkward error turns out to involve something valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOON goes inside B-ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To be baboonish is to behave like a baboon, that is loutish, gauche and ungainly.

clue.text: What identifies him includes start of petulance, bristly

indicators.note: the opening letter alone of the next word is taken
the first part holds the other inside it

blocks.note: his ID, an identity card that proves who he is
the first letter of petulance

explanation.surface: A man's identity papers mention a petulant, prickly character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What identifies him' is a cryptic way of saying his identity card, read literally as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispid is a botanical and zoological term for being covered in stiff hairs.

clue.text: Playing team games, requiring guts

blocks.note: a batter who is playing is in
sides are teams in games

explanation.surface: Taking part in team sports demands courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' tempts as courage, but here it means the internal organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Insides is informal for the stomach and bowels, like guts.

clue.text: E.g. McGonagall, larger part of destiny saved to the end

indicators.note: the bigger share of the word is the chunk that gets moved
the moved chunk is held back and placed last, so the word rotates

blocks.note: karma is fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A famously bad poet's fate was mostly reserved for the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The larger part, KAR, of KAR-MA moves to the back. William McGonagall was a Scottish poet famed as the worst in the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Makar is the Scots word for a poet, and McGonagall was a Scottish poet.

clue.text: Energy put into family's lives stimulated movement

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the other part

blocks.note: kin is family, with the possessive S
E is the symbol for energy
is means exists, lives

explanation.surface: Energy injected into a family's lives got them moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lives' is the verb, meaning exists, not the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinesis is the biological term for movement of an organism in response to a stimulus.

clue.text: I say contract's to be rewritten, ensuring inviolability

indicators.note: rewriting the words recasts them, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone insists a contract be redrafted so that it cannot be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrosanctity is the quality of being too sacred to be violated, which is inviolability.

clue.text: Cup (old) that is found in fashioned horn

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it afresh, so the letters are reordered
one part lies inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of horn, rearranged
yt is an archaic written abbreviation of that

explanation.surface: An ancient cup is found inside a carved drinking horn.
explanation.walkthrough: YT, from the old scribal form where Y stood for the letter thorn, goes inside the shuffled horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyton was an ancient Greek drinking vessel, often horn-shaped.

clue.text: Large part of tomahawk may be unearthed here

definitions.text: Large part of tomahawk may be unearthed here

indicators.note: most of the following word is kept, with its edges trimmed

blocks.note: the run of letters inside the word, with only its ends lost

explanation.surface: Archaeologists might dig up a Native American axe here.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Omaha, Nebraska, is named after the Omaha people, so their tomahawks could be dug up there.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is a city in Nebraska on land of the Omaha nation, a plausible site for buried Native American artefacts.

clue.text: This will be imbibed in some do copiously

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of some, all of do and the start of copiously

explanation.surface: Plenty of this will be drunk at a lavish party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' is a party. 'Imbibed' does double duty: the wine is drunk, and it is taken in by the clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux wine, something to be drunk.

clue.text: Rock tunes – Dominican initially involved was not in the habit

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters are tossed into a new order
involved means taken inside, so one letter sits within the rest
only the first letter of the preceding word is used

blocks.note: the letters of tunes, rearranged
the first letter of Dominican

explanation.surface: A Dominican friar used to have nothing to do with rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside the jumbled tunes, USE-NT. 'Rock tunes' looks like a music genre but 'Rock' is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Usedn't is a contracted form of 'used not', meaning did not habitually.

clue.text: Small group as is proper with end of concert given encore

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: due means fitting or proper
the last letter of concert
an encore repeats, so the letter is played again

explanation.surface: A small ensemble, as is fitting, gives an encore at the end of a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Duett is an old spelling of duet, a group of two performers.

clue.text: Hat material? Third of sale goes in a rush

indicators.note: the third letter of the next word is used
one letter enters the other part

blocks.note: tule is a large bulrush of the American West
the third letter of sale

explanation.surface: Milliners' fabric is sold in a frantic rush at the sale.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside TULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is a fine silk net, used for veils and trimming hats, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Boiled egg? It's e.g. old toying with this scoff

indicators.note: boiling churns things about, so the letters are mixed
the abbreviation and old together with the answer make up the mixed words, so taking them away leaves it

blocks.note: the letters of boiled egg, which also hold the answer
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a boiled egg as stale, toying with it.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: boiled egg is a jumble of 'e.g. old' plus the answer, so remove those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To gibe is to taunt or jeer, the same as to scoff at someone.

clue.text: I'd urge breaking with Europe, as fashion dictates (9, two words)

indicators.note: the words break apart and their letters regroup in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
EUR is an abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: A Brexiteer urges a split from Europe as the trend of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: De rigueur is a French phrase for what etiquette or current fashion demands.

clue.text: Fine glazed fabric put up

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up reads it from bottom to top

blocks.note: ciré is fabric given a glazed, shiny finish

explanation.surface: A delicate shiny material is hung up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective for the fabric but is the noun: an eric was the blood-fine in old Irish law.
explanation.definitionFit: Under early Irish law an eric was compensation paid by a killer to the victim's kin, a penalty or fine.

clue.text: Work on copy of Hockney's head – a female

indicators.note: the head of a name is its first letter

blocks.note: to edit is to revise written copy
the first letter of Hockney

explanation.surface: Someone retouches a reproduction of a David Hockney portrait of a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a girl's name, so it can stand for one female person.

clue.text: T junction of routes with lane is spanned by it

indicators.note: at a junction only the meeting ends of the two roads count, so the far parts are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written; only its tail survives at the join
taken as written; only its head survives at the join

explanation.surface: A T-shaped road junction where a route meets a lane is crossed by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T junction' reads as a road layout, but T stands alone as the definition. Butt the two road words together, routes then lane, and the answer bridges the join.
explanation.definitionFit: T is the SI symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density.

clue.text: Excludes human agency from boosters misguidedly I installed

indicators.note: something done misguidedly goes astray, so the letters wander out of order
a letter installed is fitted within the rest

blocks.note: the letters of boosters, rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly fitted booster rockets, removing the human crew.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside the jumbled boosters, ROBOT-SES.
explanation.definitionFit: To robotise a task is to hand it to machines, so people are no longer involved in it.

clue.text: Special production of Cenci, spectacular

indicators.note: a new production restages the piece, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for special
the letters of Cenci, rearranged

explanation.surface: A special staging of Shelley's play The Cenci is spectacular.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cenci is a verse tragedy by Shelley, which makes 'production' read as theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic describes a striking view or stage spectacle, so it can mean spectacular.

clue.text: Nasty nippers, group of six playing around with son joining in

indicators.note: playing around means fooling about, so the letters scramble
one letter joins in, going inside the rest

blocks.note: a sestet is a group of six lines, its letters here rearranged
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Six naughty children fool about, a son joining in their game.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside the rearranged sestet. 'Nippers' looks like British slang for children but means biting insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsetses are African biting flies that carry sleeping sickness, very unpleasant biters.
